reason: Both traps confirmed empirically in this Git Bash, and both are new (0 hits in rounds 30-43 and CONTEXT). (a) Sourcing under a pipe loses state: '. f | cat' left Y=[] and g not found, while '. f' alone kept both. Bash-tool statelessness is stated in the tool spec. (b) 'type msg' -> /c/WINDOWS/system32/msg, so an undefined msg helper runs msg.exe. One overstatement: msg.exe only targets sessions on the local machine; it is not a network broadcast. The worst case is a local popup or a 'no session' error that could be mistaken for a sent push. It is harmless to Kaggle but still worth avoiding. No script in the scratchpad (*.sh, r44dry/*.sh) still calls a bare msg. Sleep inside a sourced block works, so the 60 s retry is not blocked by the harness. One GAP in the action: the block's worst case is selread (timeout 90) + sleep 60 + selread (timeout 90), about 240 s. That is above the Bash tool's DEFAULT 120 s timeout, and no command block sets the tool timeout. On a slow or failed first SELECTED read, the call would be killed mid-retry and all state and output lost, and the R43-A3 fallback line would never print. Value is ops only (0 LB gain); it protects the 18:37Z card and the 19:43Z/21:05Z checks. It fits R1-R10: no build, no submit, 0 extra Kaggle calls.
fix: Keep the action as written: source readtime.sh on its own line, never under a pipe, in the same Bash call as cardcmd, cardfix and pushtext44; never define an ad-hoc 'msg'. To look at output, run the block and grep a file written by 'tee' in a later call, never pipe the source line. ADD: pass the Bash tool parameter timeout=600000 (at least 300000) on every readtime.sh call, because the worst case is ~240 s against the default 120 s. If a call is killed anyway, treat it as a FAILED READ under R43-A3 and re-source the block in a fresh call (1 more read_selected call, 2 in total max).
realistic_gain: 0 on public/private LB (ops hygiene only). It avoids a lost or garbled exp89t read push or 18:37Z card when state drops or the call times out (~240 s worst case vs the 120 s default), and a stray msg.exe popup. The chance that this matters tonight is small (it needs a slow SELECTED read), but the fix costs nothing.
